halt_handoff.text:
Loop 15 ended at HALT_LOOP_CAP - I made 15 loops, the configured maximum, and the backlog still has 2 items I did not fully resolve.

Where PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs stands: it began this run at 2,010 lines, peaked at 2,125 lines during intermediate work, and closes this loop at 1,987 lines (Get-Content .../PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs).Count) - net -23 from the pre-run baseline, -138 from the run's own peak. Tests grew from 167 to 206 across the run. architecture_quality moved 7.5 -> 9.0 (stuck at 7.5 across 19 critic passes before loop 10's first successful extraction); simplicity closes at 10 after this loop's own fix and a fresh full-file sweep found nothing further.

Progress so far: architecture_quality 7.5->9.0, simplicity ->10 (this loop), test_strategy 167->206 tests (8.5, unmoved for several loops on the same named Authority-Map gap), state_management/credibility holding at 10, domain_modeling/framework_idioms/concurrency holding at 9.5 with named accepted residuals.
Never moved: data_flow (held at 7.5 for the entire 15-loop run - re-derived fresh every single loop against current source, never found an actionable, SPT-passing fix; five classes hold documented process-lifetime static ambient state and converting them to instance-based DI fails Simplify Pressure Test for a single-instance desktop-widget process).

My re-derived assessment of what remains extractable versus what is a genuine floor: loop 14 named two candidates for this loop to investigate - (a) ReplaceImageCoreAsync/RestoreBackupCoreAsync's residual I/O sequencing, and (b) FixLibraryAsync's grid/portrait/icon fallback chain. I investigated both fresh against current source this loop. Neither is a same-loop slice: (a) is StorageFolder/BitmapImage/UpdateSharedEntriesAsync I/O orchestration with a single status-text ternary as its only decision logic - nothing left to extract; (b) is three shape-different, sequentially network-gated branches (the grid branch probes up to 5 ranked candidates for corner-fill via DownloadBestTileFillingImageAsync, the icon branch downloads exactly the top-ranked candidate via a different primitive, and the portrait branch is already its own extracted method) - forcing them into one shared helper would fail Simplify Pressure Test Q3 (duplicate layer for something that is not actually duplicated), the same reasoning loop 14 used to reject consolidating ShowGridPanelAsync/ShowSearchPanelAsync. The genuine remaining floor is that GameEntry itself carries BitmapImage/Visibility presentation members (TESTING.md's own documented reason PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs has no desktop test projection), which pulls every method touching a GameEntry back into the XAML-bound app container. If you want to continue past this: the concrete redesign is a plain GameRecord domain type without UI members, with LoadGameEntriesAsync/FixLibraryAsync/ReplaceImageCoreAsync/RestoreBackupCoreAsync's decision logic operating on it and a thin GameEntry wrapper left in the widget solely for BitmapImage/Visibility/INotifyPropertyChanged - introduce the type, then migrate one bulk-operation method at a time, keeping GameEntries' binding working throughout. That is a multi-loop program with real regression risk against the recorded network-call-ordering constraint if rushed, which is exactly why it was not attempted in this loop's remaining budget.

Current Priority 1 (carried forward):
  - F-022: Continue PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs's monolith decomposition via the GameRecord/view-model split named above - real, multi-loop, actionable with more budget the same way loops 10-15 have been landing sequenced slices.
  - F-011: Parallelize LoadGameEntriesAsync's per-entry network resolution - BLOCKED, not a budget question. The recorded standing user constraint (no behavioural oracle for per-game network-call ordering/concurrency changes against SteamGridDB/GOG/Epic/Ubisoft) means no loop, however many are budgeted, can land this without your explicit sign-off that an observable change in per-game network-call ordering/concurrency is acceptable.

Next step options:
  (a) Bump cap and resume - "/contest-refactor --cap 20" (or another number) continues the GameRecord/view-model split incrementally, the same sequenced way this run has worked since loop 10.
  (b) Accept current state - 15 loops moved architecture_quality 7.5->9.0, simplicity to a clean 10, and tests 167->206 with zero regressions across the whole run; the remaining monolith concern is real but now has a named, falsifiable remedy rather than a line-count guess.
  (c) Answer F-011's blocking question directly - tell me whether an observable change in per-game network-call ordering/concurrency against SteamGridDB/GOG/Epic/Ubisoft is acceptable, and I can act on F-011 in a future loop without re-litigating the constraint.
  (d) Reset - "/contest-refactor --reset" archives this halt and starts fresh from current source.

builder_notes.pattern: When a prior loop names two candidates for 'what to investigate next' and both turn out to fail the Simplify Pressure Test, the honest write-up is not 'no progress' - it is 'both candidates ruled out, here is the source-backed reason for each,' which is itself real information for whoever picks up the backlog next.
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: A finding's minimal_correction_path names two or more specific, unconfirmed candidates for a future loop, each with enough specificity (exact method names) that investigating them is verification work, not rediscovery.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Read every named candidate fully before rejecting or accepting it; cite the specific shape difference (different primitives, different call counts, different gating) that makes consolidation fail SPT Q3, not a general 'looks different enough' impression.
builder_notes.stack_example: C#: FixLibraryAsync's grid branch calls DownloadBestTileFillingImageAsync (probes up to 5 ranked candidates for corner-fill) while its icon branch calls DownloadAndReplaceImageCoreAsync directly on the single top-ranked candidate - different primitives, not a superficial naming difference.

builder_notes.pattern: A duplication fix can turn up a second, smaller bonus once you actually look at both call sites side by side.
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: A local variable is computed once and used only to feed the exact ternary being replaced - checking whether it has any other use in the method before leaving it in place.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: After replacing a duplicated expression with a call to its existing owner, grep the enclosing method for every other use of any local variable the old expression consumed - if none remain, delete the now-dead local too.
builder_notes.stack_example: C#: RestoreBackupAsync's imageFileName local was only ever used to feed the old ternary; once DisplayName(game) replaced it, the local had zero remaining uses and was deleted, while RestoreBackupCoreAsync's own imageFileName local was kept because it still fed three other calls.

builder_notes.pattern: A 'structural ceiling' claim is only as good as the remedy it names. A line-count guess is not falsifiable; a named coupling and a named redesign are.
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: A finding's proof text says something like '~N lines is probably the floor' with no specific type, member, or coupling cited as the reason.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Replace any line-count-based floor claim with the specific member(s) (type, property, or dependency) that force co-location, and name the concrete refactor that would remove that coupling - even if it is out of scope for this loop.
builder_notes.stack_example: C#: this run's earlier '~1,600-1,800 line floor' guess was replaced this loop with GameEntry's BitmapImage/Visibility members (the specific coupling) and a GameRecord domain-type split (the specific remedy).

builder_notes.stack_example: Three claims this loop's critic is least confident about: (1) simplicity's move to a clean 10 - the leaf-module duplication sweep covered PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs in full and StoreNameLookup.cs/AsyncLazyCache.cs, but did not extend to every Services/ file (ArtworkRanker.cs, ArtworkDownloader.cs, TileImage.cs, ArtworkSignature.cs were not re-read this loop) - a stricter critic doing that full sweep might find something this loop missed, though none of those files have ever been the source of a simplicity finding in this run's 15-loop history. (2) architecture_quality holding at 9.0 rather than moving to 9.5 as an accepted residual - this loop chose to keep F-022 as a genuine backlog item (queued) rather than promote it to an accepted residual, on the reasoning that a real remedy exists and just needs more loop budget than this run has left; a stricter critic could argue that since no candidate passes SPT within a single loop's blast-radius discipline, the honest score is 9.5-accepted with the redesign as a 'won't fix within this run's terms' residual, not a live backlog item that will sit unexecuted. (3) FixLibraryAsync's fallback-chain rejection (candidate b) - the 'shape-different branches' argument is sound for the grid-vs-icon comparison, but this loop did not separately stress-test whether the counting pattern (if (downloaded) successCount++; else errorCount++;, appearing near-identically in both branches) is itself worth a two-line extraction; it was judged too small to matter, but that judgment call could go either way.

narrative: Place, not win. This is the run's final loop, and it did two things honestly rather than one thing optimistically: it landed the one real, ready-to-land item on the board (F-024, RestoreBackupAsync/RestoreBackupCoreAsync now calling the DisplayName helper instead of re-deriving its formula, with a small bonus dead-code deletion found along the way), and it spent real investigation time on both of loop 14's named F-022 candidates rather than assuming either was a slice - finding that neither is, for source-backed, specific reasons rather than a shrug. architecture_quality holds at 9.0 because the honest remedy for the remaining monolith concern is a domain/view-model split, named concretely this loop (separating GameEntry's BitmapImage/Visibility members from a plain domain record) rather than restated as a vague line-count estimate - a genuine improvement over this run's earlier '~1,600-1,800 line floor' framing, and a redesign this run's remaining budget cannot safely execute in one pass, particularly given the standing constraint against changing observable per-game network-call behavior. simplicity reaches a justified 10 after a fresh full-file sweep found nothing left to fix beyond the one item just closed. Runtime ownership and concurrency both stay trustworthy: this loop's own diff touches zero fields, zero locks, zero await ordering. Tests do not reduce regression risk for this loop's own diff (it sits inside the same XAML-bound carve-out as everything else in this file), but the 206-test suite and the independent implementation review both re-confirm nothing else moved. The two items closing this run in the backlog are named plainly rather than glossed over: F-022 is real, multi-loop, and actionable with more budget; F-011 is real but genuinely blocked on a decision only the user can make.
